title: Merricks
summary: Merrick territory is remembered across the southern part of Long Island, from the Rockville Centre area toward the western Oyster Bay line, with ties to necks, bays, and south-shore places. Older histories say the Merrick people moved east from the western end of Long Island into a landscape shaped by Massapequa power and tribute relationships. Those accounts are colonial-era interpretations; Merrick place names, community presence, and documented land relationships remain the focus here.
map_geometry_source: Restored from prior WP Go Maps Merrick Ancestral Land polygon for broad community and territory context; not a village, shell-heap, burial, or private-property location.
why_this_matters: As European settlements rapidly expanded across western Long Island, the Merrick people were forced to uproot their communities and migrate eastward into unfamiliar territories. Tracing these early, coerced migrations reveals the relentless pressures of colonial development while highlighting the profound resilience of Indigenous groups who constantly adapted to survive.
